Re: Appeal of pre-service denial for hip arthroscopy  
Member: Reese Grant  
Member ID: W386277495  
Plan: Aetna Commercial/ACA  
Reference number: POC-AC94C7BBDE-82539  
Requested procedure: Hip arthroscopy with femoroplasty  
CPT: 29914  
Notice date: August 1, 2026  

To Aetna Appeals:

I appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29914. The denial states that the submitted documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I request that Aetna reopen and approve this pre-service request after reviewing the enclosed supplemental documentation.

Aetna’s publicly available Clinical Policy Bulletin 0736, Hip Preservation Surgery, identifies CPT 29914 as arthroscopic hip surgery with femoroplasty for treatment of a cam lesion. The policy’s medical-necessity requirements, as applied to femoroacetabular impingement, are addressed by the clinical records as follows:

1. Confirmed femoroacetabular impingement and labral pathology

The June 15, 2026 MRI arthrogram documents an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement. It also documents an alpha angle of 68 degrees. This supplies imaging evidence of both the labral pathology and cam morphology supporting the requested femoroplasty.

2. Symptoms and functional limitation

The patient has had 18 months of progressive hip pain that has not resolved with rest. The pain is sharp and located in the anterior groin, and it is aggravated by sitting and pivoting. The patient cannot run or squat. These symptoms substantially limit normal and recreational activities and are consistent with symptomatic femoroacetabular impingement.

3. Positive clinical examination

The orthopedic examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain. The treating surgeon, Reyes, MD, can provide any additional detail needed regarding the specific impingement maneuvers and findings.

4. Failure of conservative treatment

The patient has completed 18 supervised physical-therapy visits from April 20, 2026, through June 29, 2026. The therapy focused on core and hip stabilization, together with activity modification, and is documented in the physical-therapy discharge note.

The patient also used NSAIDs for four months with inadequate relief. A corticosteroid injection on April 11, 2026, produced only two weeks of partial relief. Thus, the patient has undergone supervised therapy, activity modification, medication treatment, and injection treatment without adequate or durable improvement. The conservative-treatment period documented in the records extends beyond 12 weeks, and the formal supervised physical therapy alone lasted 10 weeks with 18 completed visits.

5. Absence of advanced arthritis and preservation of joint space

The June 15, 2026 MRI arthrogram documents preserved joint space and Tonnis grade 0. These findings support the absence of advanced osteoarthritis and clinically significant joint-space loss.

6. Other relevant clinical information

The records document no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and no smoking. These findings do not explain the patient’s symptoms or provide a clinical reason to deny the requested procedure.

The original submission may not have included every item needed for review. Please consider the enclosed MRI arthrogram report, physical-therapy discharge note, treatment history, injection record, medication history, examination findings, and the surgeon’s supporting statement as supplemental documentation for the medical-necessity review.

If Aetna believes any specific criterion remains unmet or any particular document is missing, please identify that criterion and document in writing rather than treating the request as generally incomplete. Please also provide the clinical rationale and records relied upon for the denial, including the precise criteria applied to this case.

Based on the documented cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, anterosuperior labral tear, alpha angle of 68 degrees, prolonged symptoms, functional impairment, positive examination findings, failure of conservative treatment, and preserved joint space with Tonnis grade 0, I request reversal of the denial and approval of CPT 29914.

Please process this as a timely appeal received within 180 days of the August 1, 2026 denial notice. Please send the appeal determination in writing to the address on file and provide a copy to Reyes, MD.

Sincerely,

Reese Grant
